question: The concept of sustainable development became popular after which report (1987)? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (17/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: Rio Report
Earth Report
Brundtland Report
Kyoto Report
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Brundtland Report

Explanation:
The concept of sustainable development gained global popularity after the publication of the Brundtland Report in 1987, also known as "Our Common Future." This report was prepared by the United Nations World Commission on Environment and Development, chaired by Gro Harlem Brundtland, then Prime Minister of Norway. It defined sustainable development as "development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs." The report laid the foundation for the 1992 Rio Earth Summit and the 2015 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Other options: Rio Report relates to 1992, Kyoto Report to climate change. Thus, the Brundtland Report is credited with popularizing the term.

☛ Alternate name of Brundtland Report → Our Common Future
☛ Chairperson of the commission → Gro Harlem Brundtland
☛ Report that defined sustainable development → Brundtland Report
☛ Year of Rio Earth Summit → 1992

question: India’s National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) originally aimed to reduce particulate pollution by what percentage by 2024–25 compared to the 2017–18 baseline? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (25/03/2026) Shift 2)

60–70%

Explanation:

question: How often does India submit its Biennial Update Reports (BURs) to the UNFCCC? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (16/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: Every two years
Every three years
Every year
Every five years
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Every two years

Explanation:
India submits its Biennial Update Reports (BURs) to the UNFCCC every two years. These reports are mandatory under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change and include information on greenhouse gas emissions, mitigation actions, and support received. The purpose of BURs is to enhance transparency and track progress in addressing climate change. India submitted its first BUR in 2016. The reports also highlight actions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) and state-level plans. The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change prepares the BURs.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ How often are BURs submitted to UNFCCC? → Every 2 years
☛ When did India submit its first BUR? → 2016
☛ What does BUR stand for? → Biennial Update Report
☛ What is the main purpose of BURs? → Reporting GHG emissions and mitigation actions
☛ Which ministry prepares India's BURs? → Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

options_hi: प्रत्येक दो वर्ष में
प्रत्येक तीन वर्ष में
प्रत्येक वर्ष में

Explanation:
भारत UNFCCC को हर दो वर्ष में अपनी Biennial Update Report (BUR) प्रस्तुत करता है। यह रिपोर्ट जलवायु परिवर्तन पर संयुक्त राष्ट्र फ्रेमवर्क कन्वेंशन (UNFCCC) के तहत एक अनिवार्य प्रस्तुतीकरण है, जिसमें देश अपने ग्रीनहाउस गैस उत्सर्जन, शमन कार्यों और समर्थन प्राप्त आदि की जानकारी देते हैं। BUR का उद्देश्य पारदर्शिता बढ़ाना और जलवायु परिवर्तन से निपटने में प्रगति की निगरानी करना है। भारत ने अपनी पहली BUR 2016 में प्रस्तुत की थी। यह रिपोर्ट जलवायु परिवर्तन पर राष्ट्रीय कार्ययोजना (NAPCC) और राज्य कार्ययोजनाओं के तहत उठाए गए कदमों को भी दर्शाती है।

question: On which date was Engineers’ Day observed in India in 2025? (RRB Technician Grade III (09/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: 14 September
15 September
16 September
13 September
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 15 September

Explanation:
Engineers' Day in India is observed annually on 15 September. This day commemorates the birth anniversary of the legendary Indian engineer Sir Mokshagundam Visvesvaraya, who was awarded the Bharat Ratna. He was born on 15 September 1861 in Muddenahalli, Karnataka. Sir Visvesvaraya is regarded as one of the pioneers of modern engineering in India. He contributed to several major projects, including the Krishna Raja Sagara dam and the Visakhapatnam port. The date of Engineers' Day remains fixed every year, so in 2025 it was celebrated on 15 September as usual. The day honors the contribution of engineers to nation-building and inspires future generations.

question: In September 2025, the Supreme Court of India reaffirmed which important legal position under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989? (RRB Technician Grade III (09/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: The grant of anticipatory bail is absolutely barred if the FIR prima facie discloses an offence under the Act
The accused can apply for anticipatory bail under all circumstances
The anticipatory bail provision has been removed from the Indian Penal Code
The anticipatory bail may be granted only by the High Court
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The grant of anticipatory bail is absolutely barred if the FIR prima facie discloses an offence under the Act

Explanation:
In September 2025, the Supreme Court of India upheld the constitutional validity of Sections 18 and 18A of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989. These sections provide that if the FIR prima facie discloses an offence under the Act, the grant of anticipatory bail is absolutely barred. The Court held that this restriction protects the objectives of the Act and safeguards SC/ST communities from harassment. This decision came in the case of Sunil Kumar Upadhyay vs State of Uttar Pradesh (2025).

question: Which of the following initiatives was introduced in India during Union budget 2020-21 to support farmers by enabling efficient air transportation of agricultural produce across domestic and international routes? (RRB Technician Grade III (06/03/2026) Shift 3)

question: In which year did India sign the World Trade Organization (WTO) Agreement and become a founding member of WTO? (RRB Technician Grade III (09/03/2026) Shift 2)

Explanation:

question: Under the 2018 amendments in Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) policy approved by the Cabinet, the maximum Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) permitted under the automatic route in Single Brand Retail Trading (SBRT) is _____ (RRB Technician Grade III (06/03/2026) Shift 1)

question: Marathi belongs to which of the following language families? (RRB Paramedical (11/03/2026) Shift 2)

Dravidian
solution:

Explanation:

Marathi evolved from Maharashtri Prakrit, an ancient Prakrit language. Its literary form developed after the 13th century. Therefore, it is not related to the Dravidian, Austroasiatic, or Tibeto-Burman families.

question: What is the main objective of granting classical language status to certain Indian languages? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (18/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: To replace modern languages in education
To promote research and preservation of ancient linguistic heritage
To reduce the use of regional languages
To make them compulsory official languages
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is To promote research and preservation of ancient linguistic heritage

Explanation:
The main objective of granting classical language status to certain Indian languages is to promote research and preservation of their ancient linguistic heritage. This status is awarded to languages that have a rich and ancient literary history, dating back at least 1500-2000 years. Under this status, the central government provides financial assistance for the preservation and promotion of these languages, including establishing study centers in universities, funding research projects, and digitizing ancient manuscripts. Currently, six languages have classical status: Tamil, Sanskrit, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, and Odia. The goal is not to replace modern languages in education or reduce regional languages, but to conserve ancient linguistic heritage.

question: Which of the following deities is primarily worshipped during Chhath Pooja? (RRB NTPC Tier I (09/04/2016) Shift 3)
options: Lord Ganesha
Lord Shiva
Goddess Lakshmi
Lord Surya
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lord Surya

Explanation:
Chhath Pooja is a major Hindu festival primarily dedicated to Lord Surya (the Sun God) and his wife Chhathi Maiya. This festival is mainly celebrated in Bihar, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh, and parts of Nepal. During the four-day festival, devotees observe a nirjala vrat (fast without water) and offer arghya to the setting sun. The Sun is considered a bestower of health and life energy, and thus worshipping him brings health and prosperity. Other options like Lord Ganesha, Lord Shiva, or Goddess Lakshmi are not the primary deities of this festival.
